title: You May Be Taking Isabgol Wrong: Four Combinations That Serve Different Health Purposes
excerpt: A fitness coach breaks down how pairing psyllium husk with cold milk, curd, lemon water or hot water targets acidity, digestion, cravings and constipation differently.
body:
• Isabgol (psyllium husk) works differently depending on what you mix it with — cold milk for acidity, curd for stool consistency, lemon water for cravings, and hot water for constipation.
  • Fitness coach Priyank Mehta shared the four combinations in a viral Instagram video, explaining the science behind each pairing.
  • Psyllium is mainly cultivated in northern India and has been used as a digestive aid in Indian households for generations.
  • Each combination leverages isabgol's water-absorbing properties in a different way, targeting specific gut and digestive concerns.

More Than Just a Spoonful in Water

In Indian households across the world, isabgol occupies a familiar spot in the medicine cabinet — that small packet of pale, fibrous husk that comes out when digestion goes sideways. The default remedy: stir a spoonful into water and drink it down.

But fitness coach Priyank Mehta argues that this one-size-fits-all approach misses the point. In a recent Instagram video that has drawn widespread attention, Mehta breaks down four specific isabgol combinations, each targeting a different health concern. The logic is simple: what you mix it with changes what it does in your body, according to NDTV Food.

"In a recent Instagram video that has drawn widespread attention, Mehta breaks down four specific isabgol combinations, each targeting a different health concern."

What Is Isabgol?

Isabgol, also known as psyllium or ispaghula, is a type of soluble dietary fibre derived from the seeds of plants in the Plantago genus. The seeds produce mucilage — a gel-like substance that gives psyllium its characteristic ability to absorb water and expand.

The plant is mainly cultivated in the arid regions of northern India, particularly Rajasthan and Gujarat, making India the world's largest producer and exporter of psyllium husk. It has been a staple of Indian home medicine long before it was repackaged as a fibre supplement in Western health stores under brand names like Metamucil.

The Four Combinations

1. Isabgol With Cold Milk — For Acidity

According to Mehta, mixing isabgol with cold milk helps form a protective lining in the stomach. The cooling effect of milk combined with the mucilage layer can reduce irritation caused by excess stomach acid. For those who experience acid reflux after meals, this combination targets the root discomfort rather than just adding bulk to the digestive tract.

2. Isabgol With Curd — For Better Stool Consistency

This combination pairs isabgol's water-absorbing properties with the natural probiotics in curd. While the husk regulates excess water in the intestines, the beneficial bacteria in curd support gut flora. Mehta suggests this pairing for people whose primary concern is irregular bowel movements rather than outright constipation.

3. Isabgol With Lemon Water — For Late-Night Cravings

For those who find themselves reaching for snacks in the evening, Mehta recommends isabgol with lemon water. The fibre expands in the stomach and sends a satiety signal to the brain, helping suppress the urge to snack. The lemon adds a mild flavour that makes the combination more palatable than plain water, while the fibre provides lasting fullness without calories.

4. Isabgol With Hot Water — For Constipation

The most traditional combination — and the one most people default to — is isabgol with hot water. Hot water accelerates the hydration and expansion of the husk, which adds bulk to stool and stimulates bowel movement. This remains the most widely recommended use of psyllium as a dietary fibre for constipation relief.

A Household Staple, Refined

None of these combinations are medical prescriptions. But for the millions of Indian families who have kept isabgol in their kitchens for decades, the distinction between mixing it with cold milk versus hot water is the kind of practical knowledge that gets passed down — or, in this case, shared on Instagram. The takeaway is straightforward: isabgol does not have to be a one-trick remedy. The combination you choose should match the problem you are trying to address.
